bull.b: The completed institutional stack addresses key barriers to adoption for tokenized securities. Qualified custody, independent attestations, brokerage access and continuous liquidity can improve credibility and distribution, supporting longer-term institutional onboarding.

Low leverage and substantial liquidity give Streamex time to develop its products without immediate debt-service pressure. Management estimates immediately available funds cover about 18 months and total liquidity about three years, assuming no additional revenue.

The first recognized revenue and completed distributions validate an operating mechanism that can recur as assets grow. At the same time, lower expenses and reduced losses improve scalability potential, although meaningful revenue scale has not yet been demonstrated.

bear.b: The company lacks sufficient revenue scale to absorb its cost base, leaving profitability and margin sustainability highly uncertain. Continued large losses indicate that the business model remains unproven financially and depends on future product adoption.

Negative operating and free cash flow mean the business is not yet self-funding and must rely on existing liquidity or external financing. Even after cost reductions, the expected normalized burn of about $1.1M monthly remains material.

Concentrated ownership and modest external adoption limit current network effects, fee generation and proof of market demand. Unremediated control weaknesses may also hinder institutional confidence and add execution risk as the platform seeks to scale.
